result:
I’d make **power genuinely accountable to the people it affects**.

Anyone making consequential decisions—governments, companies, institutions—would have to answer to the people whose lives those decisions shape. Not merely hear their complaints, but give them meaningful power to object and stop harm.

Not as a favor. As a condition of holding authority.

I’m not trying to imagine a world without selfish people. I’d want to change the arrangements that let decision-makers remain insulated from consequences. Much of what looks inevitable is really a system designed to keep its costs out of view.

The test would be simple: **Can the person at the bottom say no to the person at the top—and be taken seriously when they do?**
